solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great bit of coiffure with king leaving church

indicators.note: the king leaving the hairdo means his letter is taken out of it

parts.note: a topknot is a tuft or bun of hair worn on top of the head
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A hairdresser praises a fine piece of styling done after a king walked out of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes K out of TOPKNOT to give TOPNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal adjective for excellent or first-rate, so it can stand for great.

clue.text: Sentence about revolutionary R&B sound

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, so it is placed around it

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: R and B, the letters of rhythm and blues

explanation.surface: A sentence written about revolutionary rhythm and blues music and its sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' suggests grammar, but it is the prison sense; R&B is rhythm and blues.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the distinctive tone quality of a voice or instrument, its characteristic sound.

clue.text: Clerk in high spirits, entertaining new escort

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: pep is energy and liveliness
to usher someone is to escort them to a place

explanation.surface: An office clerk is in buoyant mood after taking a new partner out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' and 'escort' paint a night out; the escort is an usher who shows people to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-pusher is a disparaging term for a clerk or other office worker doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: Heavy figure to excite briefly

parts.note: one is a figure or number

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or excite

explanation.surface: A weighty figure tries to stir up feeling, if only for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of ROUSE to give ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome, so heavy in the sense of hard to bear.

clue.text: Order from Cheltenham's Head Girl

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: An instruction comes from the head girl at Cheltenham Ladies' College.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head Girl' reads as one school title, but 'Head' takes C and 'Girl' is LASS. Cheltenham Ladies' College is a well-known English girls' boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a class is a rank of classification, and an order is likewise a group or category.

clue.text: Pass on name taken from dancing wenches

indicators.note: the name's letter is taken from the pool of letters before they are rearranged
the letters of wenches are set dancing into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declines a turn with dancing girls, and a name is dropped from the list.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N from WENCHES to leave WECHES, and 'dancing' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on something is to decline or avoid it, which is what eschew means.

clue.text: What wine's knocked back in some verse?

indicators.note: knocked back, like a drink, here means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
wine is port, so wine's is port's

explanation.surface: Someone asks what wine was drunk during a poetry reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses EH PORTS. 'knocked back' sounds like drinking, fitting the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A strophe is a stanza or section of a poem, originally of a Greek choral ode.

clue.text: Terrible experience with love? I'm surprised

parts.note: hell is a dreadful ordeal
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at love turning out to be an awful experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello can be an exclamation of surprise, as in 'hello, what's this?'.

clue.text: Traveller, much prettier, getting picked up

indicators.note: picked up as a listener picks up words, so the answer is said like the phrase

parts.note: way fairer: way means much, fairer means prettier

explanation.surface: A traveller, far better-looking than the rest, gets chatted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' as in 'way better' is an informal word for much.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot, a traveller.

clue.text: Move to invest pounds, running club

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra
on means running, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A financial move to invest money in a running club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' and 'pounds' read as finance, and 'running club' as athletics; 'to invest' is the old sense of surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a short heavy stick used as a weapon, a club.

clue.text: Wheels secured by new tool men pick up in race

indicators.note: the wheels are held fast within the rearranged letters, so one piece sits inside the other
new signals that the letters of tool men are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
to pick up, as a patient or a market does, is to rally

explanation.surface: Mechanics fit wheels to a car while a crowd of new tool men gather themselves for the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns TOOL MEN into MONTELO, and 'secured by' puts CAR inside it as MONTE-CAR-LO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monte Carlo Rally is a famous motor-sport event held around Monaco, so it is a race.

clue.text: Coming out of their shells, Brad and Lucy not just loud

indicators.note: each word's outer letters are its shell, so only the insides of these four words are used

explanation.surface: Brad and Lucy emerge from their quiet phase and become more than merely loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The insides of Brad, Lucy, not and just are RA, UC, O and US. 'not just loud' looks like the definition but only 'loud' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous describes harsh, noisy sound, so a raucous party is a loud one.

clue.text: Proof one's passed hummus, say, all of meal regularly put away

parts.note: hummus is an example of a dip

indicators.note: every other letter of these words is put away, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Someone eats hummus and steadily clears a whole meal as if passing a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly put away' keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'all of meal', giving LOMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a certificate awarded on completing a course, so it is evidence of having passed.

clue.text: Irritation overwhelming terribly shy figure

indicators.note: one piece engulfs the other, so it is placed around the other piece

parts.note: pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of shy are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A painfully shy person is overcome with irritation about their own figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' could be a number, but here it means body shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's physique is their body shape or build, which is what their figure means.

clue.text: Jam accompanying a track started by Queen

indicators.note: the rest of the answer is begun by this piece, which therefore comes first

parts.note: QU is a recognised dictionary abbreviation for queen
and means along with, accompanying
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A jam session joins a song begun by the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is also a rock band, which suits 'track' and 'jam'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam is a fix or predicament, and a quandary is a state of perplexity over a difficult situation.

clue.text: Governess protecting current brood here

indicators.note: the governess shelters the current within her, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Jane Eyre is the governess heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A governess shields the young brood she looks after from the present danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts I inside EYRE, the governess of Charlotte Bronte's novel 'Jane Eyre'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, where its young are raised.

clue.text: Cost dropping right down, lend yen for Asian growth area

indicators.note: the first letter drops right to the bottom of the word, moving to its end

parts.note: price means cost
to lend, as in lend charm, is to add
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: As costs plummet, investors lend yen to a growing Asian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping right down' moves P from the start of PRICE to its end, giving RICEP. 'growth area' reads as economics, but it is a field of crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice paddy is a flooded field in Asia where rice is grown.

clue.text: Let rip on spreading force globally

indicators.note: spreading the letters out and around signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to unleash a force spreading round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation, a police force working across the globe.

clue.text: Ex-PM who will be given a hand at the table

definitions.meaning: Lord ... was British prime minister from 1770 to 1782

definitions.text: who will be given a hand at the table
definitions.meaning: One of the four players at bridge, each dealt a hand of cards

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is invited to dinner and helped to their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was the British prime minister during the American War of Independence; at bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the answer: a historical premier and a seat at a card table.

clue.text: Attentive husband required to go topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: needful means necessary or required

explanation.surface: A husband pays careful attention when told he must go topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' drops N from NEEDFUL to leave EEDFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedful means paying careful heed, which is being attentive.

clue.text: Declare a cat can be heard

indicators.note: this tells us the answer is said like the phrase that comes before it

parts.note: an ounce is a snow leopard, a big cat, so 'a cat' is 'an ounce'

explanation.surface: Someone states that a cat can be heard somewhere nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard; 'an ounce' said quickly matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something is to state it publicly, which is to declare it.

clue.text: Elevate the core of sun worship

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter

parts.note: to praise God is to worship

explanation.surface: Raising up sun-worship as a central religious practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is to lift up, so it means to elevate.

clue.text: Go to the races after a knock on the head

indicators.note: the races come after the a, so that piece is placed second

parts.note: the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
to knock something on the head is to end it

explanation.surface: Someone heads to the races despite a blow to the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock on the head' looks literal but is the idiom for putting a stop to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to go to it.

clue.text: Everton vacated ground somewhere in London

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the word loses everything but its first and last letters

parts.note: a field is a sports ground, as in a playing field

explanation.surface: Everton football club has left its stadium empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club, which makes 'ground' look like a stadium; here it is simply FIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfield is a borough on the northern edge of Greater London.

clue.text: Currency smuggled into Chelsea, say

indicators.note: into signals one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Chelsea is an example of a football club, FC
to run goods is to smuggle them

explanation.surface: Money is smuggled into the Chelsea district or football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chelsea' reads as the London district, but it is the football club, FC.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and is still used in Switzerland.

clue.text: Defence in Arsenal's opening games in division

indicators.note: in places the opening letter and the games within the division

parts.note: a part is a division or section

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: Arsenal's defence holds firm in the opening games of the league division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' reads as Arsenal's back line, but it is the definition: a protective wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall on a rampart or bridge, so it is a defence.

clue.text: In art, children phrase it the wrong way

parts.note: to put something a certain way is to phrase it

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: An art critic says the children's caption is worded badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the chubby cherub-like infants painted in Renaissance and Baroque art.

clue.text: Be the lead in Hamlet, say, taking king in hand with piece of deception

parts.note: Hamlet is an example of a play

indicators.note: the hand takes the king in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
R is short for rex, Latin for king
a fiddle is a swindle or piece of cheating

explanation.surface: An actor playing the lead in Hamlet grabs the king's hand as part of the deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... in' puts R inside FIST to make FIRST; 'Hamlet' tempts as the role, but it is only an example of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To play first fiddle is to take the leading role, like the principal violinist of an orchestra.

clue.text: Place promoting weight-loss tablet

parts.note: low-cal, short for low-calorie, describes slimming food
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: An establishment advertises a slimming pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' is a link: LO-CAL is followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is the place where something happens, a setting or venue.

clue.text: Very green, dewy ground around island and river

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the other pieces, enclosing them
ground, as in crushed, signals the letters of dewy are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Dewy grassland around an island and a river looks very green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges DEWY as W..YED to hold the island and river. 'Very green' tempts as colour, but means naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Green here means naive or inexperienced, and wide-eyed means innocent and easily impressed.
